title: Reliability Is Not Free in Universal Quantum Work Extraction
abstract: Universal work extraction shows that input-state knowledge is unnecessary to attain the asymptotic free-energy rate. We ask whether this first-order universality extends to reliability, the exponential decay rate of extraction failure. In the work-battery fidelity formulation, we prove that no phase-independent Gibbs-preserving protocol can retain the state-aware Gibbs-preserving exponent throughout a coherent qubit time-translation orbit: at every positive target rate, its worst pointwise exponent is bounded by the corresponding state-aware thermal-operation value. The proof first establishes an exact finite-blocklength identity between phase-robust Gibbs-preserving extraction and state-aware thermal extraction. A trigonometric Remez inequality then upgrades this minimax identity to a pointwise theorem by ruling out exponential localization of the worst phase. For an explicit coherent-qubit family, known-phase Gibbs-preserving extraction is error free, whereas every phase-independent protocol has a finite worst-pointwise exponent. Thus input-state knowledge can be irrelevant to the first-order work rate yet indispensable for optimal exponential reliability.
summary: This theoretical work examines the limits of quantum work extraction reliability by comparing state-aware versus phase-independent protocols. It proves that while the average energy extracted (work rate) can be universal regardless of input knowledge, achieving optimal exponential reliability requires retaining precise knowledge of the system's initial state. The findings highlight a critical gap between these two measures of performance.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the first-order universality observed in asymptotic quantum work extraction extends to reliability, which is characterized by the exponential decay rate of failure.
main_result: Input-state knowledge can be irrelevant for the average work rate but remains indispensable for achieving optimal exponential reliability bounds.
method: The authors use finite-blocklength identities and apply a trigonometric Remez inequality to upgrade minimax optimization problems into pointwise theorems regarding error exponents.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum work extraction from a coherent qubit time-translation orbit using a two-level work battery, comparing state-aware protocols against phase-independent ones.
